cultural.vision_reason: This is a heavily embroidered woman's dress with beadwork, cowrie shells, Afghan coins (1968-1981), and bells—a classic style of ethnic dress from Afghanistan/Pashtun regions, consistent with traditional Pashtun women's garments.

physical.title: dress
physical.summary: Woman's dress. Decorated with silk embroidery, glass beads, buttons, cowrie shells and coins, including gul-i peron discs. Rust-coloured printed velvet skirt and green floral-printed cotton sleeves. Sleeves worked in pink, mustard, red and grey embroidery and cuff edges are decorated with metal stamped disks and blue glass beads. The heavily embroidered bodice is covered in multi-coloured glass beads, pearly buttons, cowrie shells, coloured embroidered panels, four different Afghan coins dating from 1968-1981, beaded tassles and bells. There is a shallow pocket on the right-hand side with beaded gul-i perons disks. The hem is decorated with patterned rows of silver metallic trim to a height of 17 cm. There is a printed purple cotton panel on the back.
